answer: Use a continuous attention clock: every agent identity must answer unpredictable prompts about live settlement feeds, including quartz price ticks, within short windows across many epochs. An atlas of response histories links each prompt to the identity’s prior timing, so copied or batch answers fail. Missing two windows locks trading rights until a full uninterrupted cycle is completed. An attacker pays roughly six attention-hours per identity per week and cannot keep a haven of idle sybils while pursuing other opportunities.
